action: Position the probe at the superior aspect of the liver. Sweep the beam through the top intercostal space.
interpretation: Initiate the scan at the top of the liver to visualize the superior margin.

action: Slide the probe inferiorly to the next rib space. Perform another sweep through this specific intercostal window.
interpretation: Systematically interrogate the liver parenchyma through the next intercostal acoustic window.

action: Continue sweeping through the intercostal space.
interpretation: Capture the image of the dome of the right liver lobe.

action: Jump the probe down to the next inferior rib space.
interpretation: Acquire a view of the main portal vein.

action: Hold the view within this intercostal window and optimize for vascular structures.
interpretation: Visualize the main portal vein as it splits into the right anterior and right posterior portal veins.

action: Move the probe to the last rib space.
interpretation: Identify the upper pole of the right kidney positioned against the liver surface.

action: Maintain the view of the hepatorenal interface.
interpretation: Judge and compare the echogenicity of the liver parenchyma relative to the kidney cortex.

action: Rotate the probe to a coronal orientation.
interpretation: Evaluate the span of the liver to check for enlargement (hepatomegaly).

action: Scan the inferior tip of the liver and the inferior pole of the kidney simultaneously.
interpretation: Confirm that the right kidney and the liver tip terminate at approximately the same level.

action: Maintain a continuous sweeping motion throughout the examination.
interpretation: Ensure dynamic interrogation of the tissue.

action: Sweep through the entire liver volume completely.
interpretation: Ensure full coverage of the organ to rule out any missed pathology.
